mainTopic: Defending רב's claim that שיעורין, חציצין and מחיצות are הלכה למשה מסיני, then the width needed to lower a too-high מבוי beam
overview: On the previous amud, רב said that שיעורין, חציצין and מחיצות are a הלכה למשה מסיני. The גמרא challenged this by reading the פסוק 'ארץ חטה ושעורה' as a list of the Torah's measures. This amud finishes that list. תאנה is a גרוגרת for carrying on שבת, רמון is the hole that breaks a vessel, זית is the כזית used for most measures, and דבש is a large date for יום הכיפורים. The גמרא then answers that the measures are really a הלכה למשה מסיני and the verse is only a hint (אסמכתא). Next it challenges חציצין from the פסוק 'ורחץ את כל בשרו'. It concludes that the oral law teaches the details of majority, minority and being מקפיד, following רבי יצחק, and that we do not make a גזירה לגזירה. Then it challenges מחיצות from the ten טפחים of the ארון and כפורת. The answer depends on רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר, and for רבי מאיר the oral law teaches גוד, לבוד and דופן עקומה. Finally the גמרא returns to a מבוי beam higher than twenty אמה, where רב יוסף and אביי disagree about how wide the raised floor must be. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Fig: the measure for carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The word תאנה in the פסוק hints to the גרוגרת measure for הוצאה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Fig' teaches the measure of a dried fig for carrying out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through the פסוק word by word. The word 'fig' hints to the size of a dried fig, which is the amount of food you must carry on שבת to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who carries food from one domain to another on שבת is only liable if he carries at least a dried-fig amount. Here the fig in the פסוק is brought as a Torah source for this measure. The point is to challenge רב's claim that the שיעורין are הלכה למשה מסיני. Step 7 answers that challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Fig, one of the seven species in the פסוק
A dried fig, used as a measure of size
Carrying from one domain to another on Shabbat

phrases.english: 'Fig': like a dried fig, for carrying out on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: You are only liable for carrying food on Shabbat if it is at least a dried-fig amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof from the previous amud. The גמרא challenged רב's claim that שיעורין are הלכה למשה מסיני by saying they are written in the Torah ('ארץ חטה ושעורה'). It began the word-by-word reading there with חטה, שעורה and גפן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The size of a גרוגרת, which is the minimum for liability for carrying food on שבת, is hinted to by the word תאנה.

steps.title: Pomegranate: the size of a hole that makes a vessel broken
steps.stepSummary: The word רמון hints to the משנה that a homeowner's vessel counts as broken when it has a hole the size of a pomegranate.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Pomegranate' teaches a measure, as we learned in a משנה: all vessels of homeowners have their measure as pomegranates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word, 'pomegranate.' It brings a משנה that uses a pomegranate as the size of a hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wooden vessel that is טמא becomes טהור once it is broken, because a broken vessel is no longer a vessel. An ordinary homeowner's vessel counts as broken only when the hole is as big as a pomegranate. A homeowner keeps using a vessel even with smaller holes, so a smaller hole does not end its status as a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Pomegranate
As we learned in a משנה
Vessels belonging to ordinary homeowners
Their measure

phrases.english: 'Pomegranate': as we learned in a Mishnah:
All vessels of homeowners
phrases.notes: Wooden vessels that are טמא and become טהור once they break.

phrases.english: their measure is like pomegranates.
phrases.notes: Only a hole the size of a pomegranate makes the vessel count as broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: רִמּוֹן כְּדִתְנַן כׇּל כְּלֵי בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים שִׁיעוּרָן כְּרִימּוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next word in the same פסוק, same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pomegranate-sized hole that makes a homeowner's vessel טהור is hinted to by the word רמון.

steps.title: Olive: a land whose measures are olive-sized
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ארץ זית שמן' is first read as 'a land all of whose measures are כזיתים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A land of olive oil (and honey)' means a land all of whose measures are olive-sized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the words 'a land of olive oil' as meaning that this is a land whose measures are olive-sized. This first wording says 'all' measures, and the גמרא is about to challenge that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea here is that the כזית is the standard measure of the Torah. The wording 'all of its measures' is too broad, and that sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Olive oil, meaning olives that produce oil
Like olives, the כזית measure
Its measures

phrases.english: 'A land of olive oil (and honey)':
phrases.notes: The word in parentheses is part of the פסוק. Its own measure is explained in step 6.

phrases.english: a land all of whose measures are like olives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ זֵית שֶׁמֶן אֶרֶץ שֶׁכׇּל שִׁיעוּרֶיהָ כְּזֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase in the פסוק, but this time it is stated as a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כזית is presented as the measure of the land, first worded as covering 'all' measures.

steps.title: Challenge: not all measures are olive-sized
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'all' measures can be כזית when it has just listed many other measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think 'all of its measures'? But there are the measures we just mentioned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the word 'all.' It points to the list it just gave, which has measures that are not olive-sized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat, barley, a רביעית, a dried fig and a pomegranate were all just given as measures, and none of them is a כזית. So the claim that 'all' measures are כזית contradicts what the גמרא itself just said. The challenge is aimed only at the wording, not at the idea that the כזית is an important measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? A way of rejecting an idea
But there are!
That we said

phrases.english: 'All of its measures' — could that enter your mind?!
But there are those that we just mentioned!
phrases.notes: This refers to the measures of wheat, barley, a רביעית, a dried fig and a pomegranate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'all' from step 3 by pointing to the earlier steps of the list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: the list itself contains measures that are not כזית, so 'all' cannot be right.

steps.title: Correction: most measures are olive-sized
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording to say 'most of its measures are כזית.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: a land most of whose measures are olive-sized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing one word. It replaces 'all' with 'most.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most Torah measures really are a כזית. Examples are eating forbidden foods and the טומאה of a dead body or a נבלה. The other measures in the list are exceptions to that general standard. The fix keeps the main idea and just makes the wording accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: introduces a corrected version
Most, the majority

phrases.english: Rather, say:
a land most of whose measures are like olives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא אֶרֶץ שֶׁרוֹב שִׁיעוּרֶיהָ כְּזֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzMaskana: Most measures are a כזית. The other measures in the list are exceptions.

steps.title: Honey: a large date for יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: The word דבש, meaning date honey, hints to the measure of a large date for eating on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Honey': like a large date, for יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פסוק with 'honey.' Here honey means dates, and it hints to the large-date measure for eating on יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'honey' of the פסוק is date honey. A person who eats on יום הכיפורים is only liable if he eats the amount of a large date. This last word completes the list of measures hinted to in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Honey. Here it means date honey, so it refers to dates
A large date, used as a measure
Yom Kippur, the fast day

steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק of the seven species maps onto measures. חטה is for a בית המנוגע. שעורה is for a bone. גפן is a רביעית for a נזיר. תאנה is a גרוגרת for carrying on שבת. רמון is the hole that breaks a homeowner's vessel. זית is the כזית, which covers most measures. דבש is a large date for יום הכיפורים.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דבש' here is not bee honey. It means date honey, which is why the measure is a date.

phrases.english: 'Honey': like a large date
for Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: This is the minimum amount of eating that makes a person liable on יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final word of the פסוק, which completes the list of measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The large-date measure for eating on יום הכיפורים is hinted to by the word דבש.
steps.whyThisMatters: With this, every species in the פסוק has been tied to a measure. This completes the גמרא's challenge, begun on the previous amud, against רב's statement that שיעורין are a הלכה למשה מסיני: the measures seem to be written in the Torah. The next step answers this challenge.

steps.title: The measures are not truly written; the רבנן leaned them on verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier challenge. The שיעורים are not really written in the Torah. They are הלכה למשה מסיני, and the רבנן attached them to verses as hints.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think the measures are written in the Torah? Rather, they are laws given to משה at סיני, and the Rabbis leaned them on verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. All the hints we just saw (רמון, זית, דבש) are only 'leanings' on verses. They are not real sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the verse 'ארץ חטה ושעורה' seems to be a Torah source for the שיעורים, so they cannot be הלכה למשה מסיני. The answer is that the measures were truly given orally at סיני. The verse only serves as a memory peg (אסמכתא), so רב's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Halachic measurements (כזית, כותבת, etc.)
A law given orally to משה at סיני, not written in the Torah
A verse used as a 'support' or hint for a law that really comes from elsewhere
Verses

steps.whatToRemember: The שיעורים are הלכה למשה מסיני. The verse 'ארץ חטה ושעורה' is only an אסמכתא, a hint and not a source.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting the earlier hints. The hints are still valid as hints. The גמרא is only saying they are not the real source of the law.

phrases.english: And can you really think the measures are written in the Torah?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical question, which rejects the premise of the challenge

phrases.english: Rather, they are oral laws (from Sinai),
and the Rabbis leaned them on verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the long reading of 'ארץ חטה ושעורה' by explaining that it is only an אסמכתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the verse as an אסמכתא rather than a true source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the verse hints to each measure, the measures must be written in the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The measures are הלכה למשה מסיני. The verse is only a support.

steps.title: Interpositions seem to come straight from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's claim that חציצין are הלכה למשה מסיני. It shows that the verse 'ורחץ את כל בשרו' teaches that nothing may block the water. The same verse also teaches the size of a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Interpositions are from the Torah! As it says, 'And he shall wash all his flesh in the water.' This means nothing should block between his flesh and the water. 'In the water' means the water of a מקוה. 'All his flesh' means water that his whole body can go into. How much is that? A cubit by a cubit, three cubits high. And the Sages calculated that a מקוה holds forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next item on רב's list, חציצין. It argues that this law is written in the Torah, so it cannot be a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'את כל בשרו' teach that the water must touch all of the body with nothing in between. That is exactly the law of חציצה. The same verse even gives the size of a מקוה (40 סאה), so it seems everything here comes from the Torah. That leaves no room for an oral law from סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: Interpositions: things that block water from touching the body during טבילה
From the Torah itself
A ritual bath used for purification
A cubit (about the length of a forearm)
A volume measure; a מקוה needs forty of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic Torah source for both the 40-סאה size of a מקוה and the basic ban on חציצה in טבילה.

phrases.english: Interpositions are from the Torah!
As it is written: 'And he shall wash all his flesh in the water' (Vayikra 15:16),
meaning that nothing should interpose
between his flesh and the water.
'In the water' means in the water of a ritual bath.
phrases.notes: 'The water' implies specific, known water

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל בְּשָׂרוֹ״ — מַיִם שֶׁכׇּל גּוּפוֹ עוֹלֶה בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: 'All his flesh' means water that his entire body can go into,
and how much is that?

phrases.aramaic: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְּרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: A cubit by a cubit, at a height of three cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁיעֲרוּ חֲכָמִים מֵי מִקְוֶה אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה.
phrases.english: And the Sages calculated the water of a ritual bath at forty se'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שיעורים, the גמרא moves to the next item in רב's list, חציצין, and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement (quoted by רבי חייא בר אשי) that the laws of חציצין are הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse explicitly teaches that nothing may block the water. A law written in the Torah cannot also be an oral law from סיני.

steps.title: The oral law is needed for hair, like רבה בר רב הונא's ruling on knots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the הלכה למשה מסיני is needed for hair. It follows רבה בר רב הונא: one knotted hair blocks, three knotted hairs do not, and two are left in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The oral law is needed for his hair. This is like רבה בר רב הונא, who said: one hair tied in a knot interposes. Three do not interpose. Two, I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The verse covers the body, but the special law about hair needed an oral law from סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'בשרו' (his flesh) teaches about skin, not hair. So the oral law adds that knotted hair can count as a חציצה. רבה בר רב הונא gives the details. A single knotted hair can be tied tight enough to block water. Three hairs cannot be tied that tightly. He leaves two as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: For his hair
A single hair (strand)
Tied (in a knot)
Interposes; blocks the water
I do not know (an open doubt)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule may seem backwards: why does one hair block but three do not? A single hair can be knotted very tightly so water cannot get in. A knot of three hairs stays looser, so water seeps through.

phrases.english: Where the oral law was needed was for his hair.
And this is like Rabba bar Rav Huna,
for Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
A single hair tied in a knot interposes,
three (tied together) do not interpose,
two, I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by limiting the oral law to hair.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: the oral law covers a case (hair) that the verse does not cover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse covers all חציצה, so there is no need for an oral law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse covers the body. The הלכה למשה מסיני adds the law of knotted hair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר רב הונא: one knotted hair is a חציצה, three are not, and two are a doubt.

steps.title: Hair is also learned from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A ברייתא learns from the extra word 'את' that hair, which is secondary to the flesh, is included in the verse. So hair is from the Torah too.
steps.simpleTranslation: His hair is also from the Torah! As a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall wash את all his flesh.' The word 'את' includes what is secondary to his flesh, and that is hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It shows that hair is also included in the verse, so the oral law still seems unnecessary. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'את' expands the verse to include things attached to the body, meaning hair. If the Torah already covers hair, then the previous answer no longer leaves any job for the הלכה למשה מסיני. רב's statement is under pressure again.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
An extra word that comes to include something more
That which is secondary or attached
Hair

phrases.english: His hair is also from the Torah,
as it was taught: 'And he shall wash [et] all his flesh':
'et' includes what is secondary to his flesh,
and that is hair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 9 by showing that hair is also included in the verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the הלכה למשה מסיני is needed for hair
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives hair from the extra word 'את'. Hair is therefore a Torah law, and the oral law again has no role.

steps.title: The הלכה teaches the details of majority, minority, and being particular
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10. The הלכה למשה מסיני is not needed to say that hair must be clean. It is needed for the detailed rules: most versus a little, and whether the person is מקפיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the הלכה came, it came to teach the rules about the majority and the minority, and about someone who is particular and someone who is not. This follows רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about hair. It says the הלכה למשה מסיני comes to teach the exact details of what counts as a blockage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'ורחץ את כל בשרו' tells us in general that nothing may block the water, even on hair. It does not say how big a blockage must be, or whether the person's attitude matters. Those details come from the הלכה למשה מסיני, so רב's statement still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה, here meaning the הלכה למשה מסיני
Most of it, the majority of the body or hair
A small part of it, the minority
Particular, minding: the person cares about the thing and would want it removed

phrases.english: When the halacha came, it came
for its majority and for its minority
and for one who is particular and one who is not particular
and in line with Rabbi Yitzchak.
phrases.notes: This points ahead to רבי יצחק's statement in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10, which showed that hair is already included in the Torah verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the role of the הלכה למשה מסיני to the detailed parameters, not the basic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הלכה was needed to teach that hair blocks, but the verse 'את' already teaches that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches the general rule. The הלכה teaches the details: majority versus minority, and מקפיד versus not מקפיד.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's rule: Torah law and two rabbinic decrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that by Torah law a blockage counts only if it covers most of the body and the person is מקפיד about it. The חכמים decreed on two more cases: most of the body without being מקפיד, and a small part with being מקפיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: By Torah law, if a blockage covers most of the body and the person minds it, it blocks. If he does not mind it, it does not block. The חכמים made a decree about a majority he does not mind, because of a majority he does mind. They also made a decree about a minority he minds, because of a majority he minds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יצחק to spell out the details that the הלכה למשה מסיני teaches. It also lists the two extra cases the חכמים added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four possible cases. The Torah counts only one as a blockage: majority and מקפיד. The חכמים added two more cases, because each one looks like the Torah case in one way, either it covers the majority or the person is מקפיד. That leaves one case with no rule yet: a minority that the person does not mind.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (not just a rabbinic rule)
Blocks; counts as a barrier between the body and the water
They (the חכמים) made a protective decree
Because of; out of concern for confusion with another case

steps.confusionAlert: 'מקפיד' is about the person's attitude toward the blocking thing, for example whether he would want it removed. It is not about the water and not about how strong the substance is. The same small speck can count as a blockage for one person and not for another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This four-way grid is the basic framework for the laws of חציצה in טבילה used in practical הלכה today.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה רוּבּוֹ וּמַקְפִּיד עָלָיו חוֹצֵץ,
phrases.english: By Torah law, if it covers the majority and he is particular about it, it blocks;
but if he is not particular about it, it does not block.
And they decreed about a majority that he is not particular about
because of a majority that he is particular about;
and about a minority that he is particular about
because of a majority that he is particular about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source mentioned at the end of step 11 to fill in the details of the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law only a blockage covering the majority that the person minds counts. The חכמים decreed on a majority he does not mind and on a minority he does mind.

steps.title: Why not also decree on a minority that he does not mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים did not also decree on the fourth case, a small blockage the person does not mind. It looks like the rabbinic cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let them also decree about a minority he does not mind, because of a minority he does mind, or else because of a majority he does not mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's list. If the חכמים decreed on cases that look like the Torah case, why not decree on the last case too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth case, a minority he does not mind, looks like each of the two rabbinic cases in one way. It matches 'minority he minds' in size, and it matches 'majority he does not mind' in attitude. So, using the same reasoning, it seems it should also have been decreed.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let them decree
Also
Or alternatively

phrases.english: Then let them also decree
about a minority that he is not particular about
because of a minority that he is particular about,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם רוּבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד!
phrases.english: or alternatively because of a majority that he is not particular about!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיגְזוֹר נָמֵי עַל מִיעוּטוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the completeness of רבי יצחק's list of decrees in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's statement that the חכמים decreed only on two of the three non-Torah cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fourth case resembles the two decreed cases just as they resemble the Torah case, so the same logic should require a decree there too.

steps.title: We do not make a decree to protect another decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases the fourth case resembles are themselves only decrees. The חכמים do not add a decree on top of a decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule itself is only a decree. Should we then get up and make a decree to protect a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The fourth case would only be a safeguard for rabbinic rules, and the חכמים do not make one decree to protect another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rabbinic cases were decreed because they could be confused with the Torah case. The fourth case could only be confused with those rabbinic cases, not with the Torah case directly. A גזירה לגזירה, a decree to guard a decree, is not made, so a minority he does not mind does not block at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
Shall we rise up (to act)
A decree to protect another decree, which the חכמים do not make

steps.whatToRemember: The four cases of חציצה: majority and minds it is Torah law. Majority without minding, and minority with minding, are rabbinic decrees. Minority without minding does not block, because we do not make a גזירה לגזירה. All these details come from the הלכה למשה מסיני, which supports רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'אין גוזרין גזירה לגזירה' appears throughout שס as a limit on how far rabbinic safeguards go.

phrases.english: That itself is a decree,
and shall we rise up and decree
a decree to protect a decree?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle-based limit: אין גוזרין גזירה לגזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fourth case looks like the decreed cases, so it should be decreed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cases it resembles are only rabbinic, and we do not decree to protect a decree. So a minority he does not mind does not block.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The details of חציצה (majority, minority, מקפיד) are not written in the Torah. They come from the הלכה למשה מסיני as explained by רבי יצחק, so רב's statement stands.

steps.title: Partitions seem to come from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that מחיצות are a הלכה למשה מסיני, saying they come from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Partitions? They are from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on רב's list, מחיצות, and attacks it the same way it attacked חציצה. It says partitions are already from the Torah, so why call them a הלכה למשה מסיני?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is written in the Torah does not need a separate oral tradition. So if the rules of partitions can be learned from a פסוק, calling them a הלכה למשה מסיני seems unnecessary. The proof comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Partitions or walls that mark off a separate area
From the Torah itself
An oral law given to משה at סיני that is not written in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The word מחיצות here is not a new statement. It is the גמרא repeating the next item on רב's list so that it can challenge it. Do not confuse מחיצות (partitions) with חציצין (blockages) from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Partitions? They are from the Torah!
phrases.notes: The same type of challenge the גמרא made against the other items on the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with חציצה, the גמרא challenges the next item on רב's list in the same way.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the laws of מחיצות are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is learned from the Torah, there is no need for an oral tradition from סיני.

steps.title: Proof from the height of the Ark and its cover
steps.stepSummary: The ארון was nine טפחים high and the כפורת one טפח, which makes ten. This shows a ten-טפח height makes a separate area.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: The Ark was nine handbreadths and the cover was one handbreadth. So here there are ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its challenge. It shows that the number ten for a partition comes from the measurements of the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון was one and a half אמות high. With six טפחים per אמה, that is nine טפחים, and the כפורת adds one more, for a total of ten. The שכינה rested above the כפורת and is said not to come down below ten, so ten טפחים is seen as marking a separate area. That means the ten-טפח rule of מחיצות can be learned from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy Ark in the משכן
The cover on top of the ארון
A handbreadth, a unit of measurement

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the famous rule that ten טפחים is the height needed to make a wall or a separate area, a rule that is basic to the laws of עירובין.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
phrases.notes: Introduces a known teaching as proof.

phrases.english: The Ark was nine handbreadths and the cover was one handbreadth,
phrases.notes: One and a half אמות of six טפחים each comes to nine, plus one for the cover.

phrases.english: so here there are ten.
phrases.notes: Ten טפחים is the height that marks a separate area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the Torah source behind the challenge in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the ten-טפח measure of a partition comes from the Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that the ארון was nine טפחים high and the כפורת one טפח, making ten.

steps.title: The tradition is needed according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, the אמה used for vessels was only five טפחים, so the ארון plus כפורת do not add up to ten. The הלכה למשה מסיני is needed to teach the number ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only according to רבי יהודה, who said: The cubit for building was a cubit of six handbreadths. The cubit for vessels was a cubit of five handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the tradition from סיני is needed for רבי יהודה, because by his measurements the proof from the ארון falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the ארון, as a vessel, was measured with a five-טפח אמה. One and a half אמות is then seven and a half טפחים, and with the כפורת it is only eight and a half. Since this is not ten, nothing about ten can be learned from the ארון, so we need the הלכה למשה מסיני.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
A cubit, a measurement of several טפחים
The cubit used for the building of the משכן and the מקדש
The cubit used for the holy vessels

phrases.english: It is needed only according to Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The tradition is needed for his opinion.

phrases.english: who said: The cubit for building
phrases.notes: The אמה used for the structure itself.

phrases.english: was a cubit of six handbreadths.
phrases.notes: A large אמה.

phrases.english: The cubit for vessels was a cubit of five handbreadths.
phrases.notes: So the ארון comes to seven and a half טפחים, and only eight and a half with the כפורת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 15-16 by limiting the need for the tradition to one opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the statement to one תנא's opinion (לא צריכא לשיטת רבי יהודה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ארון and כפורת add up to ten, so the rule of partitions is from the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה they add up to only eight and a half, so the ten-טפח rule needs a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: What about רבי מאיר, whose cubits make ten?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that all the אמות were six טפחים, so the ארון plus כפורת do make ten. According to him, why is a הלכה למשה מסיני needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, who said that all the cubits were medium ones, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. The answer works for רבי יהודה, but for רבי מאיר the proof from the ארון still works, so the problem comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, every אמה was a regular six-טפח אמה, so the ארון was nine טפחים and with the כפורת it was ten. That means the ten-טפח rule is learned from the Torah. So according to רבי מאיר, רב's claim that מחיצות are a הלכה למשה מסיני is still a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Medium, meaning a regular six-טפח אמה
What can be said? (a formula that reopens a difficulty)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, who said:
phrases.notes: Brings in the opposing opinion.

phrases.english: All the cubits were medium ones,
phrases.notes: Six טפחים each, for both the building and the vessels.

phrases.english: what can be said?
phrases.notes: By his measurements the ארון plus כפורת equal ten, so the challenge returns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 by showing it does not work according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the הלכה למשה מסיני is needed only according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי מאיר, all אמות were six טפחים, so the ארון and כפורת make ten. The rule is then from the Torah, and the tradition is unnecessary.

steps.title: For רבי מאיר, the tradition teaches other partition rules
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the ten-טפח height comes from the Torah. The הלכה למשה מסיני comes to teach the rules of גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, the הלכה למשה מסיני comes to teach the rules of גוד, לבוד, and the curved wall (דופן עקומה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18. Even for רבי מאיר, the הלכה למשה מסיני has a job, but it teaches different partition rules, not the number ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees that the Torah teaches the ten-טפח height from the ארון and the כפורת. However, the Torah does not teach the special ways that we treat a partition as existing even when it is incomplete. These include extending a wall up or down (גוד), treating a small gap as closed (לבוד), and treating nearby invalid סכך as part of a bent wall (דופן עקומה). These rules come from the הלכה למשה מסיני.

keyTerms.meaning: The law, meaning here the הלכה למשה מסיני
Extend: we treat a partition as if it stretches up or down to complete the needed size
Joined: a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as if it were closed
Curved wall: invalid סכך up to four אמות next to a סוכה wall is treated as part of the wall bending over

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, the הלכה למשה מסיני teaches the number ten. For רבי מאיר, the Torah teaches ten, and the הלכה למשה מסיני teaches גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three rules are basic tools used across ש״ס in the laws of סוכה, עירובין, and שבת. This line shows that they come from a tradition given to משה at סיני.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir,
when the halakha comes, it is
for extending, for joining, and for the curved wall.
phrases.notes: These partition rules are not written in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by giving the הלכה למשה מסיני a different role according to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the function of the source: the tradition teaches other rules.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the Torah already teaches ten טפחים, the הלכה למשה מסיני seems to have nothing to teach.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה למשה מסיני teaches גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה, which the Torah does not teach.

steps.title: How much must a too-high beam be lowered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the מבוי. If its beam is higher than twenty אמה and someone wants to reduce the height, how much must he reduce it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the beam was higher than twenty אמה and one comes to reduce the height, how much must he reduce it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the case of the משנה, a מבוי whose beam is higher than twenty אמה. It asks how much the height must be reduced to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam higher than twenty אמה does not make the מבוי usable for carrying. One way to fix it is to reduce the height, for example by raising the floor. The question asks how much of a reduction is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty cubits, the maximum height for a beam over a מבוי
To reduce it, meaning here to make the height lower
An alleyway that opens to the public domain

phrases.english: If it was higher than twenty cubits
and one comes to reduce it,
how much must he reduce?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וּבָא לְמַעֲטוֹ, כַּמָּה מְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about מחיצות and returns to the main topic of the beam's height.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount a too-high beam's height must be reduced.

steps.title: The question is obvious: reduce it as much as needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question. Obviously he reduces it by whatever amount brings it below twenty אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much must he reduce?! As much as he needs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the question from step 20 as too obvious. He simply reduces the height until it is no longer above twenty אמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of height to remove depends on how high the beam is, so there is no fixed number. This shows the question must be about something else, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as he needs

phrases.english: How much must he reduce?!
phrases.notes: A repeat of the question, said in surprise.

phrases.english: As much as he needs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the question of step 20 as obvious.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The wording of the question about height.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The height to remove is obvious: whatever brings it under twenty אמה.

steps.title: The real question: how wide must the raised floor be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rephrases the question. The real issue is how wide the raised section of floor must be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: how wide must it be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the question. The issue is not how much height to remove, but how wide the raised section of floor must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone raises the floor under the beam, he does not have to raise the whole מבוי. The question is how wide the strip of raised floor near the beam must be for the fix to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a corrected version
Its width, meaning the width of the raised floor

phrases.english: Rather: its width, how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected question with the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum width of the raised floor that reduces the height.

steps.title: רב יוסף says one טפח, אביי says four
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree. רב יוסף says the raised section must be one טפח wide. אביי says four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: one טפח. אביי said: four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two answers to the width question. רב יוסף requires only one טפח, and אביי requires four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the raised section must bring the height under twenty אמה. They disagree only about how wide that section must be. The גמרא will next try to explain the reason behind their disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who says one טפח is enough
An אמורא who requires four טפחים
Four, meaning four טפחים

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: one handbreadth,
Abaye said: four.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: טֶפַח, אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the width question of step 22 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: one טפח. אביי: four טפחים.

steps.title: A suggested reason: may one use the area under the beam?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a reason for the disagreement. The one who says one טפח holds that it is permitted to use the area beneath the beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they disagree about this: the one who said one טפח holds that one may use the area beneath the beam.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. The גמרא begins to suggest the basis of the disagreement and explains רב יוסף's side first. The other side continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the area under the beam belongs to the מבוי and may be used, then the beam acts like a wall at its outer edge. In that case, a narrow one-טפח raised strip under the beam is enough, because that area is already part of the מבוי. The word לימא shows this is only a proposal, which the גמרא may later reject.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say; introduces a suggestion that may be rejected
They disagree
The beam placed across the entrance of the מבוי
Beneath the beam

steps.confusionAlert: לימא is only a suggestion, not a final conclusion. The גמרא often proposes a reason with לימא and then rejects it.

phrases.english: Let us say they disagree about this:
that the one who said one handbreadth
holds: it is permitted to use
beneath the beam,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a reason for the disagreement in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggestion: רב יוסף requires only one טפח because he holds that the area under the beam may be used.
